rationale: The disease gene itself. MVA1 is dosage-sensitive: BubR1 hypomorphic mice are progeroid and aneuploid, BubR1 overexpression protects against aneuploidy, cancer and muscle/renal ageing. Raising residual BubR1 from the missense allele is the most direct compensation.

Deacetylates BubR1 K668 and prevents its APC/C-mediated degradation; NAD+ repletion (NMN) raises BubR1 in vivo. K668 lies outside both patient variants (L751*, N1016K), so the route applies to the missense protein.
Acetylates BubR1 K668, the modification that SIRT2 removes; lowering it should stabilise BubR1. No selective approved inhibitor expected.

AAA+ ATPase that disassembles the MCC; inhibition could prolong whatever MCC forms in BubR1-deficient cells. Itself an MVA3 gene, so loss is also pathogenic: dosing direction is a testable hypothesis, not established.
Core MCC partner of BubR1. Not pharmacologically modulable in the desired direction.
Recruits BubR1 to kinetochores. Inhibition would worsen the checkpoint defect.
BubR1 kinetochore adaptor (GLEBS motif). No drugs expected.
MCC target; inhibiting CDC20/APC/C could restore the mitotic delay lost with BubR1. Treated as a testable hypothesis per procedure Step 2 (only proTAME/apcin, preclinical).
APC/C cullin subunit contacted by the BubR1 TPR 'lasso'. Same caveat as CDC20.
APC/C E2 enzyme driving cyclin B1 degradation and mitotic exit.
Kinetochore MAD2 template; no drugs expected.
MPS1 inhibition is synthetic-lethal with a weakened SAC (tumour-selective killing). Would also stress the child's own SAC-weak normal tissues: selective toxicity, not rescue.
CIN-selective dependency, but requires a competent SAC to arrest; BubR1-deficient cells resist monotherapy.
BubR1 partner at the kinetochore; inhibition (GSK923295) would worsen attachment errors.
Microtubule-binding kinetochore core; no drugs expected.
Cohesin protector; no drugs expected.
Without BubR1-bound PP2A-B56, Aurora B phosphorylation is unopposed and attachments are destabilised; partial Aurora B inhibition could rebalance kinase/phosphatase activity.
Phosphorylates the BubR1 KARD to recruit PP2A-B56; inhibition would remove the remaining recruitment signal (wrong direction).
Catalytic subunit of PP2A-B56 recruited by BubR1 (LxxIxE); activation would compensate for lost recruitment. No approved activator expected.
Separase triggers anaphase once the SAC is satisfied; no drugs expected.
Aneuploid cells are proteotoxically stressed and hypersensitive to proteasome inhibitors.
Aneuploid cells depend on HSP90 chaperoning; synergy with APC/C inhibition reported.
Aneuploid cells depend on de novo pyrimidine synthesis.
POLE exonuclease inhibition reported to kill highly aneuploid lines selectively.
HIF1A inhibition lowered survival of aneuploid cells in mosaic settings.
Wnt hyperactivity in BubR1-deficient hearts. The child has no reported heart defect: low phenotype relevance.
Upstream Wnt secretion node (same rationale as CTNNB1).
Transcriptional driver of BUB1B in rhabdomyosarcoma; RMS cells depend on FoxM1/Bub1b.
Senescent-cell survival node (BCL-xL). Genetic clearance of p16+ senescent cells in BubR1 hypomorphic mice delayed sarcopenia.
Senescent-cell anti-apoptotic node (same rationale as BCL2L1).
Dasatinib target class (SRC/ABL/ephrin kinases) mediating senolysis of senescent progenitors.
Dasatinib primary target; included to capture the approved senolytic.
Senomorphic route (suppresses SASP). General senescence biology, no BubR1-specific evidence found.
ChEMBL annotates rapalogs (sirolimus, everolimus) against FKBP12, which they bind to inhibit mTORC1; added so the MTOR senomorphic route is not missed. Same caveat as MTOR.
Target of vinca alkaloids/taxanes used in RMS therapy. Their efficacy relies on a functional SAC; BubR1/SAC loss is linked to spindle-poison resistance.
